page_title: Behind the scenes: McDonald’s event-driven architecture

sources.entry: Behind the scenes: McDonald's event-driven architecture - From the McDonald's tech blog, August 2022. Not very detailed, but an easily digestible case study about event-driven architecture at scale. Listing this here is not an endorsement of their products. There's a second part, too.

summary.title: Behind the scenes: McDonald's event-driven architecture
summary.one_liner: McDonald's describes the design goals and main components (MSK Kafka broker, schema registry, standby event store, SDKs, event gateway) of its unified event-driven platform.
keywords: custom sdk for event producers and consumers
how to build eventing platform at scale
case study event streaming at scale
takeaways: A unified eventing platform gives teams a standard way to build event-driven systems, reducing inconsistency and operational complexity.
Design goals for such a platform include scalability, availability, performance, security, reliability, consistency, and simplicity.
McDonald's uses AWS MSK (managed Kafka) as its event broker, chosen for AWS integration and a balance of low operations overhead and customization.
A schema registry enforces event contracts and compatibility checks, and a standby event store prevents message loss when the broker is unavailable.
Language-specific SDKs built in-house add schema validation, error handling, and retry logic, and an event gateway handles external partner events with authentication and authorization.
summary.summary: The post is a high-level case study from McDonald's tech blog (August 2022) on building a unified platform for real-time, event-driven architectures. It explains the challenge of inconsistent implementations across distributed teams, then lists seven design goals. It then describes the main components: an AWS MSK event broker, a schema registry, a standby event store for outage protection, custom SDKs, an event gateway for partner events, and operational tooling for dead-letter topics and cluster health. It is an overview only; the implementation details are promised in a second part, and the page itself gives few technical specifics.
